A fulfilling, adventurous and inspiring education
Academic success is at the heart of a Dauntsey's education, but the ethos is about much more than exam grades. It’s about developing the skills and characteristics, such as resilience, flexibility and a willingness to have a go.
We aim to be a school where everyone can be themselves, where friendship and kindness really matter and where pupils make the most of their talents and abilities.
JP is currently one of the 1st XV coaches at Dauntsey’s, as well as heading up girls’ and Sevens rugby. He has previously played professionally for Exeter Chiefs and now holds an Advanced Rugby Coaching Award.

Having left Dauntsey's in 2019, Margot is now a Marketing Executive with Gilbert Rugby
Beatrix Fooks (OD 2024) is now studying History of Art at the University of Edinburgh.

Jolie Brise
Our world famous, gaff-rigged pilot cutter

pageCache.pageTitle: Head Master's Welcome - Dauntsey's School Wiltshire
pageCache.text:
Head Master's Welcome
Dauntsey's is a school that is focused on nurturing curiosity, building confidence, and preparing young people for a future full of possibility, and I am immensely proud to be its Head Master.
Instilling a love of learning in our pupils is central to our ambition — we want all pupils to be fully engaged in their education, encouraging them to boldly embrace every challenge, both inside and outside the classroom. We are also committed to delivering this education in a considerate and caring environment, where pupils feel relaxed, comfortable and respected.
Surrounded by Wiltshire countryside, our pupils thrive in a setting that promotes not only excellence but also mental and emotional well-being. Here, learning stretches beyond textbooks, with our extensive programme of adventurous co-curricular and academic enrichment activities that foster creativity, collaboration, and connection with the wider world.
Our commitment to blending traditional values with a contemporary education ensures that each pupil is prepared for the ever-changing demands of the modern world while remaining grounded in the core principles of respect, modesty, and compassion. We are an inclusive community that welcomes pupils from all walks of life, whether they live locally or have joined us from the other side of the world. There is a pathway here for every child to discover their true interests and talents, and grow to be the best version of themselves.
I encourage you to explore more of what makes Dauntsey’s truly special by visiting the school and meeting some of the brilliant people who call this place home – our greatest strength is our sense of community and family. And whilst the buildings, facilities, and opportunities here are truly excellent, when all is said and done it is the relationships we forge in our time here that will matter the most.
Visit Dauntsey's
We are delighted that you are considering Dauntsey's for your son or daughter. Please do get in touch with our Admissions Team who will be able to arrange a time for you to visit the school.
Contact Admissions Team
When pupils arrive into Lower School at Dauntsey's they will be part of a cohort of around 100 children who have come from over 60 different schools, state and prep, local and overseas.
Joining the Middle School (Fourth and Fifth Form) at Dauntsey's is a pivotal moment in a pupil's life.
Moving up into Sixth Form is a key milestone in any pupil’s educational journey. It is a step up academically, emotionally and socially and the Sixth Form offering at Dauntsey’s has been developed to reflect this.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision, Ethos and Aims - Dauntsey's School Wiltshire
pageCache.text:
Vision, Ethos and Aims
Vision
The school will deliver a fulfilling, adventurous and inspiring education for every pupil, in a supportive and inclusive environment.
Pupils will leave Dauntsey’s confident in the knowledge that they have achieved their very best, experienced all they could and ready for their next journey.
Ethos
Dauntsey’s is a supportive, energetic and creative community with a strong family atmosphere. It is a school where friendships, generosity of spirit and mutual respect really matter, and where independent minds, adventurous souls and socially conscious individuals thrive.
Aims
The ABCs of Dauntsey's
Ambitious
Strive to be ambitious in all areas of your life. In academic studies, aim high and be the best version of yourself. We appreciate that each individual’s goals will be different, but we ask all students to ensure that they are working to achieve the very best they can for themselves.
Brave
Try new things. Push yourself outside of your comfort zone. Do not be afraid to fail. These are all things that we encourage of our students. We often do not know what is possible, until we find out what isn’t. Bravery is something that is as important in the classroom as it is outside, and is a vital skill for success later in life.
Compassionate
Show kindness to each other, but also be kind to yourself.
A happy student is a successful student.
We are a kind community and one that is based on mutual respect.

About
Dauntsey’s is a leading co-educational boarding and day school for 11-18 year olds. Set in an estate of 150 acres of idyllic countryside, on the northern edge of Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, we offer some 830 pupils challenge and inspiration both inside and outside the classroom.
Academic success is at the heart of all that we do, but our ethos is about much more than exam grades. It’s about developing the skills and characteristics, such as resilience, flexibility and a willingness to have a go, which we all need to have a successful, happy life. We aim to be a school where everyone can be themselves, where friendship and kindness really matter and where pupils make the most of their talents and abilities.
An Adventurous Education
Central to this ambition is our approach to adventure. Adventure at Dauntsey’s is not simply an event but something that teaches invaluable life skills and changes attitudes and behaviour for the better. This spirit of adventure reaches into the classroom where inspirational teaching stretches and nurtures each pupil’s learning.
This approach ensures that we are equipping pupils with the necessary skills and confidence to succeed in whatever the future holds for them.
ISI Report 2026
In April 2026, Dauntsey’s underwent a full inspection with the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), and we are delighted that the report captures both the quality of our education and, most importantly, the strength of our community.
The full report, along with a summary, can be found here.
Embrace new adventures, be ambitious in your learning, and always be kind to yourself and others.John Davies, Head Master

Partnership Programme
At Dauntsey’s, we believe that education should inspire, empower, and open doors to a world of opportunity—not just within our own school but across the wider community.
We are committed to working in partnership with local schools and organisations to share knowledge, resources, and experiences that make a real difference to young people’s lives.
Our extensive programme of partnerships enriches learning for hundreds of pupils beyond Dauntsey’s. From academic collaborations to creative arts, sport, and outdoor education, we are dedicated to widening access to opportunities that might otherwise be out of reach. These partnerships are about more than just sharing facilities—they are about sharing inspiration, creating lasting connections, and supporting young people to discover their talents and potential.
If you are interested in supporting our Partnership Programme, or would like to find out more, please contact our Foundation Office. With your help we can open more doors, create more possibilities, and make a lasting impact on the lives of more young people in our wider community.

pageCache.pageTitle: The School Counsellors - Dauntsey's School Wiltshire
pageCache.text:
The School Counsellors
Our two School Counsellors are a confidential and trusted support for all pupils, as and when needed.
A clear distinction is made between the counsellors and the teachers. Any discussions that pupils have with the counsellors remains confidential. The only exceptions to this are if it is felt a pupil is in danger of seriously harming themselves or others, or if they agree that it would be helpful to involve someone else.
The counsellors are not just here for the big problems through, anything that is bothering a pupil enough to make them anxious or unhappy may well be helped by coming to talk about it. No pupil will ever be made to feel that their problem is not worthy of a chat.
How does it work?
Counsellors are good listeners, but counselling goes beyond that. They will try to help you become clearer about situations, feelings and thoughts. Sometimes just voicing out loud what has been going around in your head can help clarify things.
They won’t make judgements or try to give you advice or provide all the answers, but believe that through support, individuals are able to find their own solutions and develop their own strategies.
They help you sort out why things may be happening to you, what needs to change and how those changes can take place.
Pupils can access the School Counsellors through asking a Teacher, Tutor or House Parent, Nurse, Librarians or any member of the Listening Service. They are also able to email the counsellors directly, should they not wish anyone to know that they are seeking support.
Ms Ruth Archer
Mrs Carole Coupe

Bursary Programme
At Dauntsey’s, we believe that talent and ambition should be nurtured, regardless of background.
Over the past ten years, we have provided 30 full bursaries to exceptional young people who might not otherwise have had access to an education like ours. These bursaries have been truly life-changing, not only for the pupils themselves but also for the school community, which has been enriched by their talents, perspectives, and contributions.
Watching these pupils grow in confidence, seize opportunities, and go on to achieve great things has been an honour. Whether excelling academically, thriving in the arts or sport, or becoming leaders in their chosen fields, their journeys stand as a testament to the power of opportunity. Their time at Dauntsey’s has shaped their futures, and in turn, they have left a lasting mark on the school.
While we are incredibly proud of what we have achieved so far, there is so much more we can do. With your support, we can open our doors to even more talented young people, ensuring that financial barriers do not stand in the way of potential.
We look forward to sharing the stories of our bursary recipients in the future—stories of resilience, ambition, and success made possible by the generosity of those who believe in the power of a Dauntsey’s education.
If you are interested in supporting our bursary programme please get in touch with the Foundation Office.

Partnerships
Last year, every week of the school term, over 350 children took part in an outreach event organised by Dauntsey’s, be that out on the sports pitches, in the science lab or elsewhere around the site. Our partnerships are an important part of Dauntsey's life and we are continually looking to grow and expand on what we are doing.
At Dauntsey’s, we believe strongly in the importance of being rooted in our local community, as well as engaging with the wider world. Through a variety of partnership initiatives and philanthropic activity, we seek to instil in our young people the value of service and the importance of using our time and energy to make a positive difference in the lives of others. An awareness of the world around and a desire to serve others are hallmarks of a Dauntsey’s education. John Davies, Head Master
Our goal is to make a positive contribution to our local community and to really involve our own pupils in this endeavour. We want to offer opportunities for the wider community to use, and benefit from, our facilities, while also fostering relationships with many partner organisations.
Many of our programmes have run for decades, but we are always looking for ways to extend and develop outreach so that we can offer something for everyone.
A key aspect of our outreach programme is our regular sports coaching which has been running for some fifteen years. To boost primary schools’ PE provision, we visit eight local schools for weekly training sessions, practice drills and games for pupils of all abilities. Each term, we focus on a different sport – hockey, netball and kwik cricket – and then hold a festival where all schools compete against each other. It’s always a big event and a number of our Sixth Form help with umpiring and organisation.
We also are involved in a number of different partnerships with local schools and sports organisations, whereby we work to organise coaching, training events and competitions. For example, we hold an annual Mid Wilts Primary School KS2 Dance Festival, where schools choreograph a routine and then spend the afternoon at Dauntsey’s preparing for an evening performance in the Memorial Hall - in the past we have had 250 pupils from 12 schools participating.
On an ongoing basis, local schools and clubs can take advantage of our all-weather Astroturf pitches and swimming pool. Four schools and nine local organisations are currently using these facilities.
Dauntsey’s is lucky to have a 150-acre campus with woodland and open spaces - perfect for adventure. We regularly host groups at The Manor for den building and campfires as well as orienteering. We have also previously hosted the Mid Wilts Orienteering Event. We also run a programme for disabled children and other groups to take to the high seas on board Jolie Brise which makes for a truly memorable adventure.
An afternoon of fantastic fun activities in the woods! The favourite was the sausages cooked on the open fire! Would love to come again next year!
For the last 15 years we have run a Design Technology outreach programme for local primary schools. Year Six pupils are able to come in and use our computer aided design (CAD) and computer aided manufacturing (CAM) kit to build a clock which they are able to take home with them. Not only is this a memorable day, but it also helps schools to fulfil some of their national curriculum requirements. In addition, we share our facilities and expertise in a Science Week which enables local children to run experiments and become ‘mini scientists’ for the day.
Our annual Dodecahedron Mathematics Competition has been running for more than thirty years. The competition has recently been re-vamped to focus on local primary schools. The competition involves ten to twelve teams of four Year 6 pupils from each primary school and gives them the opportunity to stretch themselves beyond the normal maths curriculum, working as a team to solve various challenges. In addition, each summer the Mathematics Department runs a number of roadshow events at local primary schools, with the aim of generating enthusiasm and excitement through solving interesting problems.
Being able to tap into resources and staff expertise at Dauntsey’s has made for a very memorable few days and has really helped us to ignite a passion for science in our pupils. Phillippa Winbolt, Head Teacher, Daps Primary School, Wiltshire
Throughout the year we open our doors to the community, in particular to our wonderful drama and music performances. Our Memorial Hall is one of the largest venues in Wiltshire, with a capacity of some 900 people, and a highlight of the year is our Christmas musical, which brings in more than 2,500 visitors over its five-night run. Depending on the production, we sometimes invite children from local primary schools for behind-the-scenes tours and smaller, taster performances as well.
There is also our weekly Choral Society, open to parents, teachers and locals, who perform pieces at our Autumn and Spring concerts.
Our Mercers’ Lectures are hugely popular free events that give local people the chance to listen to a varied and interesting range of world-class speakers. We receive such positive feedback from local people who love coming to these events. Recent speakers include Ant Middleton, Steve Backshall, Lucy Worsley and Dr Bettany Hughes.
Pupils are encouraged to get involved in community service. Some join in as part of their Gold Duke of Edinburgh Award or our sports leadership programme, but many volunteer simply because they want to make a difference.
One of the options they find most rewarding is visiting local primary schools to listen to the children reading and help the teacher through our Voluntary Service Unit (VSU). VSU placements, which change each term, also include helping out in charity shops and local retirement homes.
I have loved getting to know all the children in the class that I help with. It is so rewarding to see their progress even in the short time I am there. Every week, I look forward to it more. Amelia, Sixth Former
Sport Outreach
Adventure Outreach
Events at Dauntsey's
Community Service
Charity Programmes
Dauntsey’s was founded with a charitable gift 450 years ago and in just the past decade we have raised more than £350,000 for good causes both in the UK and overseas. This charitable activity feeds into the Complementary Curriculum whose mission is to “foster the development of integrity, honesty, fairness, sensitivity, generosity, commitment, compassion and respect for self and others in the local community and further afield.” The result is a wider perspective on life and a realisation that even small actions and decisions can affect others for the better. Our annual charity fundraising programme involves all the pupils who start by choosing a charity to support. This alternates each year between UK and international causes, with each of the twelve houses running events to raise money. Pupils also raise money through sponsorship for events such as the Devizes to Westminster canoe race, a 24-hour runathon on a course through the school grounds. An important aspect of our charity work is our long-standing commitment to a Romanian Orphanage. For pupils in the Lower Sixth, there is an opportunity to travel to Romania to help at the Nightingales Children’s Project. A group of about 20 students spends a week with street children in the town of Cernavoda, playing games, dancing, organising art and craft sessions and helping with infrastructure projects, which have included building a playground. The trip is so popular that we receive nearly two applications for every place.
The pupils really get behind our chosen charity each year and are very creative with their fundraising activities. They have come up with everything from the sale of bacon butties to a lip-sync contest and an annual boules competition.
Rev Jez Barnes, Chaplain

Our Governors
Members of the Governing Body, along with short biographies, are listed below.
The Chair of the Governing Body may be contacted via the Clerk to the Governors (clerk@dauntseys.wilts.sch.uk) at Dauntsey’s School, West Lavington, Devizes, Wiltshire, SN10 4HE. If it is necessary to communicate confidentially with the Chair of Governors, correspondence marked ‘Confidential for’, should be sent to The Chair of Governors, Dauntsey’s School, West Lavington, Devizes, Wiltshire, SN10 4HE.
After reading Geography at Cambridge, I worked as an accountant and auditor in London until I retired in 2020. I and my wife live in Devizes. We have two grown-up daughters, and my hobbies include walking and climbing, researching the history of the family and the house, and owning two dogs.
With a background in accountancy, I have been fortunate enough to work in over 30 countries with a variety of private and public enterprises, and I currently work as an advisor on finance transformation with CFOs in UK and US listed businesses. In addition, I have served on a variety of boards for Wiltshire based charities, and as a Non-Executive Director within the NHS.
I am married and have two children, both of whom happily attended Dauntsey’s School, and it is an honour to maintain my association with the school as a Governor.
I spent seven happy years at Dauntsey’s as a day pupil, my family then living in Urchfont. After a brief spell in the Royal Navy I joined the Royal Hong Kong Police where I worked for nine years, leaving as a detective chief inspector working in commercial crime. Whilst in Hong Kong I studied for a London University External LLB, and having obtained it returned to London and spent the following 23 years at the Bar, specialising in professional negligence and employment law.
I became a Recorder in 2002 and a full-time Circuit Judge in 2012, and now divide my time between presiding over criminal trials in the Crown Court and sitting as a Judge of the Employment Appeal Tribunal.
As a founder member of the Sailing Club at Dauntsey’s, I spent many a day working on and sailing in Griffin II, including a crossing of the Bay of Biscay with little by way of navigation equipment other than a compass! I am currently the Commodore of the Bar Yacht Club.
I live in Godalming, Surrey with my wife, and have two married sons and two grandchildren. As well as sailing I enjoy walking, cycling, cooking and travelling.
I read History at Cambridge University and then joined J. Walter Thompson, the global advertising agency. A director since 1989, I ran blue chip accounts for clients such as Unilever, Esso, Kellogg and Nestle. Following the arrival of three sons I moved into HR, Talent Recruitment and Development with a special focus on diversity and women’s leadership. I was made a Fellow of the IPA for services to the industry in raising professional standards and developed the industry’s first apprenticeships. I now run my own consultancy specialising in brand communications and leadership coaching. I have had one son at Dauntsey’s, when, new to Wiltshire, I became an active member of the DSPA (which I can thoroughly recommend!) and established the Dauntsey's Mentor Network with the aim of bringing the world of work to life for Dauntsey’s pupils.
I live locally in Semington with my husband Richard and a variety of horses, sheep, cows and royal corgi Ruby.
After spending my early years in Surrey, I was lucky enough to move to West Cornwall for my secondary education where I also studied Rural Studies as well as learning to surf (though not very stylishly I’m afraid!). I then went on to study History at the University of York and then completed a Masters in International Relations at Bristol.
Since then, I have worked in several Independent Schools in Bristol and Bath in both academic and pastoral leadership, and am currently Deputy Head (in charge of Pupil Development) at Bristol Grammar School. I live in Bath with my partner and have two teenage children.
I joined the governing body in 2025 and am a Mercers’ nominated Governor. I am a member of the Governance, Compliance, and Safeguarding Committee.
I was educated at Gresham’s School, after which I studied English and Education at Homerton College, Cambridge University.
During my teaching career, I worked at a wide range of schools in both the maintained and the independent sectors, latterly as Deputy Head Academic of an HMC school. I have also worked for the Independent Schools Teaching Induction Panel (IStip). I am a Reporting Inspector for the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) and an educational consultant. I love working with others to help young people feel inspired by and benefit from an excellent all-round education.
I joined the governing body in 2025 and sit on the Education Committee. I am married and live in Bath. We have three grown-up sons. My hobbies include keeping physically fit to as a counter balance to the hours I sit devouring literature! I have always taken an active interest in the Arts.
My home and place of work is in Wiltshire, my extended family and that of my wife’s family are also based here. I am a Chartered Building Surveyor, educated at a local comprehensive school, technical college and The Polytechnic of Central London, graduating in 1985. My children (22 and 24) each spent seven well rounded and happy years at Dauntsey’s. My wife Sally spent her Sixth Form years there too. I became a Governor in 2020 and am a member of the Estates Committee. I am a keen swimmer of many years, for the past twenty or so particularly an open water swimmer. Kayaking and walking are my other interests which also help me to stay sane in the busy world of work.
Educated in London and later with the OU, I have lived and worked in the Middle East, Far East and North America, as a TEFL teacher and for various charities. Following my degree I worked in HR, and currently work at a local specialist dyslexia school.
My three sons went to Dauntsey’s, as did my father. I became a member of the DSPA and joined Dauntsey’s Choral Society in 2006. I was honoured to be asked to join the governing body in 2018, and am passionate about maintaining the values of kindness, confidence without arrogance, and community, that I observed as a parent when we first visited the school. I live locally with my husband Nick and our two spaniels and became Safeguarding Governor in 2022.
Thanks to a generous and life changing bursary, I was educated at Stonyhurst College and read Classics at Oxford University.
I have worked for some time in education at a very wide range of schools in both the state and independent sectors as well as internationally in Sri Lanka and Argentina. For 17 years now I have worked in leadership roles and I am currently Headmaster of Millfield.
I am a Mercers’ nominated Governor. I joined the governing body in 2021 and I chair the Education Committee. I am married and have two young children. I am at my happiest in the mountains.
I was born in Belfast, graduated in Wales and qualified as a Chartered Accountant with KPMG in Southampton before continuing south to Kenya for two years. I finally settled in Wiltshire with my wife and two sons, both of whom attended Dauntsey’s in the 2010’s.
I have worked for large companies such as BP and Aviva, but also for smaller, owner led companies, giving me diverse experience across many different businesses, including horse racing, nightclubs, renewables and vodka.
I have been an advisor to a cancer charity for almost ten years and was honored to be invited to join the governing body at Dauntsey's in 2026.
Educated at Epsom College, my professional journey culminated as Vice Chairman at Musgrave Group Plc, a 148-year-old family company in the food retail and wholesale sector. In this role, I served on the main Board as well as on the Audit, Remuneration and Shareholder Committees.
Prior to this I had run my own Estate Management Company looking after farming estates on the Marlborough Downs.
I was previously a Governor at the Royal Agricultural University for 9 years, aligning Farms strategy, overseeing projects, and contributing to environmental initiatives. A panel member for DEFRA, a Fellow of the Royal Agricultural Society, and Chair of the Marlborough Downs Nature Enhancement Partnership - I remain active in my commitment to sustainability.
I'm married to Sarah, a psychotherapist, and have two children, one who attended Dauntsey's from 2005 - 2012. I'm also a keen sailor, serve as Treasurer at Marlborough Rugby Club, and enjoy travelling..
I was educated at Cheltenham College and qualified as a Solicitor at the London law firm, Withers, in 1981. I was a partner in the Salisbury law firm, Wilsons Solicitors LLP for 38 years retiring in 2024 and served as managing and senior partner. I am now a Board director with the hospitality business, the Chickpea Group, and a consultant solicitor with Lawhive Legal and ON Consulting. I specialise in Employment law. I am an experienced non-executive director and charity trustee.
I was privileged to join the Governing Body in September 2022 and I chair the Governance, Compliance and Safeguarding Committee.
I spent seven years at Dauntsey's as a student, after which I studied archaeology at the University of Birmingham and then went on to complete a Masters in Science at the University of Edinburgh.
I have since spent 10 years working as a policy advisor on climate change for the UK government including leading negotiations on climate change at the UN. I left to advise businesses on global climate policy and now work at an NGO as Director of Public Affairs, supporting the development of high integrity carbon markets.
I'm a keen kayaker having competed in the Devizes to Westminster three times - the first time whilst at Dauntsey's. I now live in Worcester with my husband and my dog Charlie.
I joined the Governing Body in April 2024 and sit on the Estates, Infrastructure and Assets Committee.
I was educated at Charterhouse School and subsequently gained a BSc in Geochemistry from London and an MA in Strategic Studies while in Australia. I enjoyed a 30 year military career, retiring in the rank of Brigadier and then served abroad as a Director and Chief of Staff of several NATO agencies. I now undertake charity work, for the Veterans Advisory and Pensions Committee and for RE:ACT, a disaster response charity.
I am delighted to be part of the governing body as a Mercers’ nominated governor. I am a member of the Estates, and the Finance and General Purpose Committees, and chair the strategy group. I am married with two grown-up daughters and my hobbies include ski mountaineering, nordic skiing, diving, cycling and travelling.
I am a management consultant and have led and managed businesses in both the small independent sector and for large, publicly listed organisations, primarily in the IT and Software industry.
I was educated at Oundle School and attended Goldsmiths College, University of London, where I studied History. On leaving University I joined the Army and completed a short service Commission.
I am a liveryman of Worshipful Company of Mercers and have sat on number of committees that focus on the Philanthropic aims of the Company. My focus was on two elements of our philanthropy, young people and education and older people and housing. I am also on the Board of Peter Symonds Sixth Form College Winchester.
I am a trustee of Emerge Advocacy who work with young people (10-25 years old) who present in A&E with a mental health crisis.
I live with my wife Lizzie in Wiltshire and have three grown up daughters.

Pastoral Care
Pastoral care at Dauntsey’s is about striking a balance between care and personal development. We are here to help each individual to find out more about themselves, to enjoy success beyond the classroom, make lasting friendships and of course experience inevitable failures in a safe and supportive environment.
At the heart of our community is the House system, which creates a feeling of belonging and collective responsibility. However, our network of care and support reaches every corner of the school; from the teaching staff to the nurses and counsellors, the chaplain, to the domestic staff, there is an abundance of staff making sure that the mental, physical and spiritual needs of all pupils are met.
If talking to a fellow pupil feels a more comfortable option, we offer our Listening Service which was developed by a group of Upper School pupils who wanted to receive training so that they could be a first point of contact for other pupils to talk through any problems or worries.
Boarding at Dauntsey's
Our boarders are at the heart of our school community and every pupil joins one of five houses which are co-educational in the Lower School and single sex in the Upper School.
Day pupils at Dauntsey's
All day pupils, like boarders, join a house, which are mixed in the Lower School and single sex from age 14-18. The houses provide a secure source of support and guidance in every aspect of life, as well as place to get together and have fun.
Safeguarding at Dauntsey's
At Dauntsey’s, safeguarding is at the heart of our pastoral care. Our dedicated safeguarding team works closely with pastoral and medical staff to ensure the wellbeing of every pupil.
As part of the wider safeguarding system, our experienced team is trained to identify concerns early, provide support, and promote pupils’ welfare, preventing issues from escalating. The Designated Safeguarding Lead offers guidance to staff and liaises with external services when needed.
We encourage all pupils to speak openly with staff, report any concerns, and seek support. They can do this by talking to a trusted member of staff, using the Listening Service, or through Student Voice.
For current parents, further contact details are available on the Safeguarding pages of My School Portal (MSP).
A Christian ethos underpins the community and life at Dauntsey's. Our Chaplain leads Sunday and weekday services as well as a weekly service of Holy Communion.
We are lucky to have a superb Medical Centre on the School campus which is manned 24 hours a day by registered nurses.
Our two School Counsellors are a confidential and trusted support for all pupils, as and when needed.

The Chaplaincy
A Christian ethos underpins the community and life at Dauntsey's.
Our Chaplain leads Sunday and weekday services as well as a weekly service of Holy Communion. They are there to support pupils from all faiths and those of no faith with an aim is to foster deep-rooted spirituality and moral values in all of our pupils.
During the week there are services aimed to engage pupils of different age groups, and there are regular mid-week services for the whole School. The school gathers for important days such as Remembrance and the Carol Services are always a special end to the year.
Boarders have a short informal service in school most Sundays. At the beginning and end of the year there are special services at All Saints’ Church in West Lavington to which day pupils and all parents are warmly welcomed.
A Confirmation Service is held annually at Salisbury Cathedral. A preparation course is held by the Chaplain for those who wish to consider Confirmation as part of their spiritual development whilst at Dauntsey's.
Reverend Jez Barnes
Revd Jez Barnes is Chaplain to the whole Dauntsey’s community, a tutor in Fitzmaurice and a teacher of Religious Studies, Philosophy and Ethics. Prior to joining Dauntsey’s, Jez spent 24 years as a Christian Priest in three very different Anglican parishes in London. He studied Theology at Oxford University and Economics, Politics and Psychology at Southampton University. Jez also coaches cricket, football and rugby, all of which he has loved playing over the years.
Jez is married to Emma and they have three children, a cat and a dog. When not playing, coaching or watching sport, Jez enjoys family walks with the dog, reading and watching films.
“As a family who have recently moved to this area from London, we’re grateful for the warm welcome we’ve received from the Dauntsey’s community and for all the opportunities ahead to explore more of this beautiful part of the world.”

pageCache.pageTitle: The Listening Service - Dauntsey's School Wiltshire
pageCache.text:
The Listening Service
The Listening Service at Dauntsey's started over 15 years ago.
We have 28 volunteer listeners ranging from those in the Fourth Form to Upper Sixth pupils. Each volunteer receives a number of training sessions, plus a one-to-one interview, led by one of our counsellors. The training sessions focus on issues surrounding safeguarding and confidentiality, they give guidance on how to provide support and when to refer pupils to a counsellor or a member of the pastoral team. Each listener is assigned a buddy within the group so that there is someone with whom they can discuss individual cases and agree the best course of action. Nobody is left to deal with anything on their own.
Listeners wear a silver badge on their jacket or blazer to help identify them. Posters are displayed around the school with contact details for all the listeners, along with the school safeguarding leads and counsellors. Pupils can chat to listeners anywhere in the school and there is also a small meeting room dedicated to the service where they are able to meet. Topics vary widely, but often relate to stress and anxiety, homesickness and friendship issues. These can often be dealt with by the listener, but staff will step in if necessary. The listeners are helpful in feeding back to us on common threads that might emerge.
Our main objective is to provide a safe space where anyone can come and talk to us. We won't tell them what to do but talking about things can make a real difference. We sometimes feel we have nipped a problem in the bud just by having a conversation.
UPPER SIXTH STUDENT LISTENER

pageCache.pageTitle: The Medical Centre - Dauntsey's School Wiltshire
pageCache.text:
The Medical Centre
We are lucky to have a superb Medical Centre on the school campus which is manned 24 hours a day by registered nurses.
Our Junior Boarders at The Manor also have a registered nurse on from 07.00 to 08.15 every morning and again in the evening between 19.00 and 21.00.
The Medical Centre consists of four Inpatient rooms which are all en-suite with TVs and DVDs, a waiting room, sisters' office, doctor/physiotherapy consulting room, treatment room (with double door ambulance access), cosy sitting room, large kitchen and counselling room.
All our pupils both day and boarding are provided with medical care, including administration of first aid, emergency care and supervision and administration of prescription medicines and over the counter medications which are dispensed in accordance with the school doctor's advice. Parents are asked to sign that they agree to this practice on entry of a child to the school.
Communication between the Medical Centre, academic staff, House staff and parents is vitally important to ensure the wellbeing of the pupils. Pupils are always encouraged to keep parents/guardians informed of medical issues. All medical information is held in confidence by the Nursing Staff in the Medical Centre and only shared if necessary to ensure the safety of a pupil.
Day pupils have access at all times during the School day to medical advice and first aid from a registered nurse.
If day pupils are unwell they may rest in the Medical Centre before returning to lessons. If it is necessary for the pupils to go home parents are contacted by the Medical Centre and the pupil cared for until they can be collected.
In the case of an accident or injury, (external sports fixtures included), that is deemed an emergency the pupil is escorted to hospital by a member of staff. The Medical Centre will contact parents for them to relieve the member of staff at the hospital as soon as they can.
HPV and Menacwy are carried out by the Area Health Authority and consent forms are sent out prior to vaccination dates. All other vaccinations for day pupils need to be arranged through the family doctor.
All boarders will be registered with the Lansdowne Surgery in Devizes by the Medical Centre. A GP from the practice holds a surgery at School twice a week.
If the pupils need to see a doctor outside of surgery times appointments can be made at the surgery in Devizes and a member of staff will accompany them.
Inpatient care — parents are informed of an overnight or prolonged stay in the Medical Centre. Nursing Staff will also inform the Boarding Houses of pupil admissions. Parents may, of course, take their children home to recuperate should they wish.
Emergencies - in the event of an accident/injury the medical staff always attempt to contact parents but in the case of an emergency a member of staff may need to act in loco-parentis and sign for any procedure deemed necessary by the attending physician. Parents agree to this when signing the School's medical entry form.
Communication and prescription medicines - it is vital that the Medical Centre is informed of any accidents/illnesses/operations/ vaccinations that are carried out during the School holidays. Prescribed medicines should be bought to the Medical Centre on return to School to ensure that the Nursing Staff are kept up to date with treatment.
Overseas pupils must not bring their own medicines into school for their personal use unless prescribed by a Doctor. All medication must be handed over to the Medical Centre for safe keeping. Parents should be aware that some medication prescribed overseas is not licensed for use in the UK. In this case the School doctor will make an individual case assessment and offer UK licensed medicines where appropriate. It is very important that as much medical information as possible is available to the School doctor.
Medical Care for Day Pupils
Medical Care for Boarders
Vaccinations for Boarders
Travel vaccinations for boarders are organised by the Medical Centre. It is helpful if parents can give us as much notice as possible of an impending trip. Pupils who are going on a Gap Year or to Medical/Dental School may also need additional vaccinations. If this is the case, please inform the Medical Centre as early as possible as some of the vaccinations require a course of injections over a period of 6 months.
Routine Diphtheria /Tetanus/Polio vaccinations are organised for boarders. A consent form is sent to parents prior to vaccination.
Boarders with predisposing medical conditions e.g. diabetes, asthma or those who are immuno-suppressed will be offered the chance to receive the influenza vaccination. A consent form is sent to parents prior to any vaccination.
Optical/Dental Appointments for Boarders
Routine dental, orthodontic and optical care appointments should be arranged during the school holidays.
All boarders who wear glasses/contact lenses need to keep a spare pair of glasses at school for emergencies.
A physiotherapist visits the School twice a week. This can be covered by private medical insurance or the charge added to the School bill.

Performing Arts
At Dauntsey's, everyone has the opportunity to get involved in music, drama and dance, and you will find the First Form mingling with the Sixth Form, and future professionals working alongside people who simply want to get up and 'have a go'.
With concerts or recitals most weeks, six or seven drama productions every year and a major dance showcase, there is plenty of opportunity and choice.
The performing arts are among the school’s great strengths, attracting audiences of more than 500 for major concerts or shows. They are so much a part of the fabric of life here that pupils arrive for rehearsals straight off the Astro turf or out of the classroom, ready to change mental gear and take up an entirely different challenge.
Over the years I have struggled with confidence but at each audition I've gone to I've become stronger and stronger.Aurora, Sixth Form Pupil
There are many opportunities to enjoy Dance at Dauntsey's and classes are open to all pupils, both boys and girls, experienced dancers and those pupils who are new to this discipline.
Drama is thriving at Dauntsey's and the School has become well known for the high standard of its productions, all of which are open to the public.
Music plays an important part in the life of the School and whether it be academically, socially or spiritually, music touches the life of every Dauntseian.
Speech and Drama are available to pupils across the school; students can choose to study Acting, Devising or Shakespeare.
Annabel's Studio is an entirely flexible space which is used for teaching, for exam presentation work, workshops and for smaller-scale productions. It is essentially a black box that can be configured in any number of ways.
The studio is equipped with lighting and sound equipment, and sets are built to the requirements of each production. Set design is one of the options that candidates can specialise in at A Level.
Our Dance Studio is a delightful space with fully sprung floor and wall to wall mirrors into which light floods in.
The Memorial Hall, or 'Mem Hall' as it's often referred to, with its sophisticated sound and lighting system can seat up to 730 people and is the chosen venue for major productions such as the December Musical and annual Lower School Production.
This versatile space accommodates a wide range of styles and productions can be staged conventionally or in the round.
Venue 2 is the newest building added to the drama facilities. Erected in 2007, it serves as a teaching space, rehearsal room and a comfortable performance venue seating for approximately 60 people depending on the seating layout.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupils First - Dauntsey's Digital Charter - Dauntsey's School Wiltshire
pageCache.text:
Pupils First - Dauntsey's Digital Charter
Our commitment to safeguarding pupils in the digital world
At Dauntsey’s, the wellbeing, privacy and safety of our pupils are at the heart of everything we do - including how we use images online. As digital platforms continue to evolve, we believe it is essential to take a proactive, responsible approach to ensure pupils remain protected in an increasingly complex online environment.
Our Pupils First – Dauntsey’s Digital Charter sets out our strengthened commitment to safeguarding pupils across all our digital communications.
To ensure we are putting pupil safety first, we are committed to implementing a more secure approach to how and where we share images of school life.
As social media becomes increasingly complex, the responsibility schools carry in the digital space has never been greater. This charter is an important step in ensuring that our pupils are protected, respected, and fully aware of how and where their images are used.
I am proud that as a school we are taking these proactive and decisive steps to put pupils first. We remain absolutely committed to sharing the spirit and vibrancy of Dauntsey’s, but in ways that never compromise the safety or privacy of the young people entrusted to our care.
John Davies - Head Master
What this means for our community
We our committed to sharing the joy, energy and achievements of Dauntsey’s life with our families, just in ways that are safer and more controlled. Parents have access to event photography and celebrations of school life; these are simply shared in environments designed to protect pupils.
Our goal is to remain transparent, responsible and forward‑thinking in our approach to digital communication. The Pupils First – Dauntsey’s Digital Charter reflects the values that have long defined Dauntsey’s: care, community, respect and integrity.
We welcome feedback and conversation about our Charter. Please contact our Marketing & Communications team if you would like to discuss the Digital Charter further.

pageCache.pageTitle: Equality Diversity Inclusivity - Dauntsey's School Wiltshire
pageCache.text:
Equality Diversity Inclusivity
Dauntsey’s is committed to creating a fully inclusive school.
At Dauntsey’s we aim to create a friendly and supportive environment, where staff and pupils have every opportunity to fulfil their potential and achieve their aspirations, both inside and outside the classroom. An essential part of achieving this goal is the school’s active engagement with the issues of the day and the fast-changing world in which we live.
We are fortunate to have a wide range of nationalities and backgrounds at the school, with each pupil and member of staff bringing something unique to our community. But we can always learn more about the world, about ourselves, and build a better understanding of equality, diversity and inclusivity (EDI).
The views of pupils are a key aspect of our planning, with additional input from everyone in the Dauntsey’s community: staff, parents and governors.
Under the guidance of Inclusion Labs, the school is conducting an audit of our perceptions, behaviours and plans for the future. Inclusion Labs will support us in developing our action plan and the longer-term development of the programme.
We look forward to updating you on the next phase of the initiative, and we welcome any input from our Dauntsey’s community.

Our History
Dauntsey's was founded in West Lavington, Wiltshire, in 1542, under the will of Alderman William Dauntesey, Master of the Worshipful Company of Mercers.
I William Dauntesey Citizen and Alderman of the Cities of London... will that in West Lavington a house called a church house and a house for a schole be kept... and that Ambrose Dauntesey shall name and appoint one apt and convenient person to teach gramer in the Schole house...
From these humble beginnings over four and a half centuries ago, Dauntsey's has grown into a thriving, modern co-educational school with more than 860 pupils, with continued links with the Mercers' Company.
William Dauntesey
William Dauntesey, born in Wiltshire in 1483, was the youngest son of four, and went to London at an early age to try his fortune in trade. There he was apprenticed to William Lambert, Master of The Mercers' Company, and completed his apprenticeship in 1504. He was elected Master of the Mercers' in 1531, and became an extremely prosperous man, making frequent purchases of lands and houses in Wiltshire, London and elsewhere. On 10th March 1542, he signed the will by which The Mercers' Company later received his London properties, with the obligation to maintain the School and Almshouses which his executors were to build in West Lavington.
It All Began Here
The school was opened in 1553 in the old building, which still stands opposite the Church in the High Street of West Lavington. The first master was named Adam Waters.
In 1878, dissatisfaction was growing about the school, probably against the background of rising awareness of the importance of education. A group calling themselves 'The Memorialists' submitted a list of complaints about the running of the school, and they were supported by the Leader of the Commons, W.H. Smith, who delivered a powerful speech on their behalf in the House in 1887.
17 years later, a new school came into being. Joseph Chamberlain, a radical MP, prevailed upon The Mercers' Company to make available a sum of money to establish an agricultural school. This was to offer opportunities suited to a rural area, for boys of all classes, since scholarships would be available for pupils from the local elementary school, though others would be required to pay fees of £30-£50 a year.
Thus it was that the Dauntsey's Agricultural School came to be built and opened in 1895.
1895
May 7th - The Rt. Hon. Joseph Chamberlain opened the new buildings and officially inaugurated Dauntsey's Agricultural School. The Head Master was F.W. Long
1898
There were 60 boys in the school.
1900
The numbers were 37, of whom 12 were boarders. Mr. F.O. Solomon was appointed Head Master in place of Mr. F.W. Long.
1902
The School magazine was started.
1912
A new wing was added to the north end of the school. This provided a joint Museum and Library with Masters' accommodation above. The old museum was changed into a common room for indoor games. The tuck shop was instituted.
1913
Six acres of land purchased.
1914
Canadian troops were billeted in the school.
1919
Mr. F.O. Solomon retired; Mr. G.W. Olive was appointed Head Master (pictured right). Proposal to raise Boarding fees from £45 to £60 / £75. There were 67 pupils in the School.
1923
Name changed to Dauntsey's School and the first inter-house matches were organised.
1924
The Head Master's present house was built. The Assistant Master's house, new Chemical Laboratory and West Dormitory were built. The Old Chemical Laboratory was converted into the changing room.
1925
The dining room of the Head Master's old house was converted into a reading room. Fives courts were completed. A potting shed was erected by the boys.
1929
Purchase of the Manor House Estate, Market Lavington. Biological Laboratory (Farmer Laboratory) opened. Benefaction of £13,000 by the Farmer Trustees.
1930
Dauntsey's made a Public School. Name officially altered from Dauntsey's Agricultural School to Dauntsey's School. Wing added to Sanatorium, changing rooms at Manor built, Cricket scoreboard built.
1933
Farmer Hall opened, named after Mr. S.W. Farmer O.B.E., a notable benefactor, who died in 1926. New School uniform introduced. The extra accommodation provided by the New Hall enabled the old Dining Hall to be divided into two rooms, devoted to English and History respectively. The New Rest Room becomes the Modern Language Room, the Common Room and the Physics Laboratory.
1934
Manor developments: Swimming Pool, Games Room Craft Room, additional dormitory accommodation, accommodation for domestic staff (see below).
1935
Advanced Science laboratories opened. Biological gardens formed.
1936
Gymnasium built (now the Tedder Building). Exchange programme with boys from Oranienstein Gymnasium in Germany who visit Dauntsey's (pictured below).
1937
New Changing Rooms and Dormitory Block built. Enlargement of Farm Buildings. Scout Troop formed.
1938
Miniature Stadium laid out. Purchase of the remainder of Warrington Field, and levelling begun by pupils. Scout Hut erected. Kitchens modernised and extended. Marsden-Jones collection of British Plants established in Biological Gardens.
1941
Work on the land, food production and training of land girls. Domestic service rendered by staff and boys. Cycle Section of Home Guard and Air Training Corps formed. Purchase of two cottages (Prospect House). Mercers' Hall in London badly damaged by enemy action. Rhododendron and azalea avenue planted in the Manor Woods.
1945
School opts to become a Direct Grant School. Completion of levelling of Warrington Field by pupils.
1948
Sanatorium (medical centre) at Manor House completed.
1949
Building of the Garden of Peace and Remembrance commenced on the site of the present Memorial Hall. Combined Cadet Force formed.
1954
Opening of new school buildings to provide five classrooms and studies to house English, Modern Languages, Geography, History and Classics - now the Maths Department.
1955
Retirement of Mr. G.W. Olive. New Head Master - Mr. D.J. Forbes.
1957
365 pupils. Opening of New Science Building to house Physics and Chemistry, funded by the Industrial Fund for the Advancement of the Teaching of Science in Schools (£18,000 grant).
1958
Workshop built by boys. New tennis courts constructed next to the Head Master's House.
1962
Additional Biology Laboratory and Science Lecture Room opened.
1963
Completion of the engineering block, built by the pupils, now the Lower School Centre.
1967
Olive Block opened: now Fitzmaurice House.
1969
Mr. D.J. Forbes retires. New Head Master - Mr. G.E. King-Reynolds. 410 pupils. Extra playing fields to the south of the farm buildings purchased by A.E. Hemens and given to the School.
1970
New squash court built.
1971
First girl pupils at Dauntsey's - 6 girls were admitted to the Lower Sixth Form in September. Dauntsey's School Sailing Club started, acquiring use of Griffin II.
1972
Farm closed. Buildings used for School purposes. Memorial Hall building commenced on site of Memorial Gardens.
1973
Farmer Hall converted to Farmer Music School
1974
Memorial Hall officially opened.
1976
Dauntsey's began to take girls at all levels.
1977
Sailing Club acquires use of Jolie Brise, famous gaff cutter originally built in 1913.
1978
Jeanne House opened for senior girl boarders. New Classrooms developed from existing Engineering Shop. Open Air Swimming Pool in valley at Manor broken up and filled in.
1979
Conversion of Lecture Theatre and laboratories into additional Physics Laboratory. Gymnasium converted, new storey added to provide classrooms and Lecture Theatre - opened by Lord Tedder in September. New Sports Hall building commenced.
1980
March: the Awdry Sports Hall opened. Day and Boarding Houses given separate areas. Housemaster's House built on to the Olive building, which becomes Fitzmaurice House. Front of main building accommodates Dauntsey House (senior day girls), Farmer and Hemens (senior day boys).
1983
Five Courts converted into shops. Second-hand clothes and Sports Shop opened.
1985
533 pupils. Heated Indoor Swimming Pool officially opened on 13 July. Mr. G.E. King-Reynolds retires. New Head Master - Mr. C.R. Evans. 450th Anniversary of the introduction of Dauntsey's School in William Dauntesey's will.
1986
New Lower School Day Houses Scott and Rendell formed.
1987
Craft Design and Technology Centre opened.
1988
New Sanatorium (Medical Centre) built. Creation of Mathematics Block by infill on ground floor. Six Maths Rooms and Staff Room provided. Extension of Biology Labs - addition of Project Room, Staff Area and New Laboratory
1989
Two-storey extension to Science Building to provide: two Physics laboratories, Project Room/Library and Technician's room. New wing to Jeanne House (further 35 beds).
1991
606 pupils. New Boarding House for senior boys - Mercers' House opened by Mr. J.J. Fenwick Master of The Mercers' Company, providing 64 beds for pupils.
1991/1992
Refurbishment of the area vacated by Mercers' House to create 15 new classrooms for History, English, Economics, Classics and Religious Studies; five Art Studios and new accommodation for Hemens and Farmer houses.
1992
All-weather playing surface constructed.
1994
Extension to Fitzmaurice House built.
1995
625 pupils. Extension to Music School and Dining Hall. Celebration of the Centenary of the School's reopening on its present site.
1996
Retirement of Mr Christopher Evans, Head Master. New Head Master - Mr Stewart B. Roberts. Dedication of Henderson Gardens (in memory of Harry Henderson). Building of new Staff Common Room and unveiling of statue of Euterpe (designed by David Backhouse).
1998
New netball/tennis courts.
1999
New Art Department opened on old Primary School site. Opened by R.K. Westmacott Esq., Master of the Mercers' Company. The Dauntsey's Aided Primary School moves to a new purpose-built school in the village
2000
677 pupils. Opening of the new Library and IT Centre.
2002
Dauntsey's School production of 'Les Miserables', is so successful that it is invited to perform for one night only at the Prince of Wales Theatre, in the West End of London. Pupils performed to a full house, an audience of over 1,000.
2003
Biology Department, constructed in 2002, opened by OD John Rendell ('47-51'), Trustee of the Samuel William Farmer Trust. New Science Department under construction. Brown uniform phased out and replaced by the new blue uniform.
2004
Science Department opened by HRH the Duke of Kent. The new senior girls' boarding house (Evans) is completed providing accommodation for 60 girls in single and double en-suite rooms. Opening of extension to the Design & Technology Department.
2005
740 pupils. Refurbishment of old Biology Department to house the senior boys' day houses, Farmer and Hemens opened by Mr Wathen, Governor. Evans House officially opened by Robert Bernays, departing Chairman of Governors. Richard Handover, CBE, elected new Chairman of Governors. Jolie Brise leads flotilla past Her Majesty The Queen and also leads the re-enactment of the Battle of Trafalgar on the 200th Anniversary of the death of Lord Horation Nelson.
2006
Jolie Brise wins the 50th Anniversary Tall Ships' Race. Pupils take the production of 'Assassins' to the Edinburgh Fringe and receive four star reviews from the critics.
2007
Drama Studio is renovated, reopened and renamed Annabel's, in memory of Annabel Maurice (OD '96-'03). Refurbishment and extension of Fitzmaurice House completed and a major revamp of The Manor undertaken.
2008
786 pupils. Official opening of the new all weather AstroTurf pitch by Simon Mason and Richard Mantell.
2009
Jolie Brise takes part in the Tall Ships Transatlantic Challenge and wins the second leg from Tenerife to Bermuda, 1st in class and 1st overall.
2010
Over 100 senior day girls from Lambert and King-Reynold were delighted to return to School in September to their new, modern, purpose-build day house accommodation. In the Summer Term a small ceremony marked the opening of the enlarged and modernised cricket pavilion. The ribbon was cut by Lt. Col. Tim Lerwill, a long serving MCC committee member and manager of numerous MCC tours.
2011
The final phase of the Science Development Project is completed; including two new chemistry laboratories, chemical prep rooms, a chemical store, an additional teaching room and an internal courtyard garden. Jolie Brise is declared the overall winner of the Tall Ships Race Series 2011.
2012
Head Master Stewart Roberts retires after 15 years and Mark Lascelles takes over as Head Master.
2013
The School celebrates Jolie Brise’s 100th birthday and she competes in the Fastnet Race; the team of Sixth Formers were delighted to break Jolie Brise’s previous record in the race, set over 75 years ago, by 24 hours. Jolie Brise also sailed up the Thames for a reception at St Katharine Docks with Tower Bridge opening twice to let her pass. The ASTO Hammond Innes Small Ships race followed, from Ipswich to Cowes.
2015
Pupils perform Lord of the Flies – an all-boy cast of 30. Jolie Brise is overall winner of Tall Ships Races 2015 - race through the Outer Hebrides and Shetland Islands to Ålesund in Norway, 60 nautical miles south of the Arctic Circle.
2016
The school site is transformed. A new state-of-the-art Pavilion was opened, containing eight changing rooms and a triplet aspect social space capable of seating more than 200 people A new classroom block housing mathematics, geography, business studies and economics, known as The Olive Building, and an all purpose, multi-functional dance studio with a sprung floor opened.
2017
A cast of 100 pupils, supported by our own technical crew and full orchestra performed Billy Elliot at the Novello Theatre in the West End, London.
2019
An all-weather athletics track is built on Mercers’ Fields, alongside the Pavilion.
2024
John Davies joins Dauntsey's as the new Head Master.
2025
A new Sixth Form centre, including a meeting room, is created from a section of the library, adjacent to the Pig and Whistle. Other im
